subsystem: Autonomy and proactivity (awareness, cortex, goals, missions, council, forge, self-improvement)
summary: This is the part of Apex that watches your PC in the background, speaks up when something looks important, works on goals you set, runs multi-round Missions, and tries to improve itself (forged tools, self-modification, reflection, auto-rollback). Almost all of it is real code with a lot of tests (about 720 test functions), and resident mode now starts the same awareness monitor as main.py. But on your Windows laptop several pieces are weaker than the docs suggest: the active-window watcher only works on Linux, so most Guardian Angel triggers can never fire. The Council can never meet with DeepSeek alone. Anything that needs a yes/no safety confirmation is refused automatically in resident mode. The weekly self-evaluation and nightly reflection jobs are only scheduled by main.py, not by resident mode.

features.name: Awareness monitor (background watcher)
features.what: A background thread that records what you do: which window is active, what you copy, and file changes in Documents/Desktop/Downloads. Every 15 seconds it runs Guardian, Time Capsule, restraint and reflection checks.
features.how_to_use: Automatic at startup in both main.py and resident mode (AWARENESS_ENABLED=true by default). The events appear in the dashboard Logs/live feed.
features.evidence: agent/awareness.py:246-442 (AwarenessMonitor, _review_loop), build_monitor agent/awareness.py:505-590; started in main.py:383-391 and app/resident.py:227-249. The window watcher calls xdotool only (agent/awareness.py:83-99), so on Windows it fails silently every 2 s. Clipboard needs pyperclip (requirements.txt:17); files need watchdog (requirements.txt:14). Tests: tests/test_resident.py, tests/test_startup_resilience.py (startup wiring), none for ActiveWindowWatcher.
features.setup_needed: None to start it. On Windows the active-window part does nothing, because there is no Windows code path.

features.name: Proactive 'Heads up' speak-ups
features.what: Every 60 seconds, if anything happened, it sends the last 20 events to the background model (deepseek-flash for you) and asks whether something is urgent. If the model says yes, Celine says 'Heads up. ...' out loud.
features.how_to_use: Automatic. Turn off with --no-proactive (PROACTIVE_ENABLED). Guardian, cortex and Time Capsule keep running.
features.evidence: agent/awareness.py:420-441 and _proactive_check agent/awareness.py:519-540; config.py:29-31 (PROACTIVE_MODEL falls back to BACKGROUND_MODEL, i.e. deepseek-flash), config.py:87.
features.setup_needed: A working model key. On Windows it only has clipboard and file events to judge from, because window titles never arrive.

features.name: Guardian Angel
features.what: Watches for 'commitment moments': a secret pasted from the clipboard, an angry message about to be sent, a purchase, a destructive git commit, or a calendar clash. When one fires, it speaks one warning line and sends a high-priority notification.
features.how_to_use: Automatic (GUARDIAN_ANGEL_ENABLED=true). Turn it on or off from the Guardian panel on the dashboard (/api/guardian, /api/guardian/toggle).
features.evidence: agent/guardian.py:32-70 patterns, :101-170 detection uses window_title + clipboard; :286-297 speak + notify. Wired in agent/awareness.py:552-582. Dashboard routes dashboard/server.py:1037,1044. Tests: tests/test_guardian.py (15). In resident mode, dash.set_guardian() is never called (only main.py:414), so the dashboard Guardian log may stay empty there.
features.setup_needed: On Windows only the clipboard-based triggers (secrets, commit commands) can fire. Message, shopping and calendar triggers need window titles, which are Linux-only today.

features.name: World model (live context snapshot)

features.how_to_use: Set a goal (say 'set a goal to ...' or use the Goals tab). Approve or reject staged actions in the Approvals tab (/api/pending-actions).

features.name: Missions page

Missions survive a restart and keep Windows awake while they work.

gaps.issue: On Windows the awareness window watcher never sees any window. It only calls xdotool (a Linux tool), fails silently every 2 seconds, and has no Windows branch. As a result Guardian Angel's message, shopping and calendar triggers can never fire on your laptop, and the proactive 'Heads up' review only sees clipboard and file events. agent/app_context.py has a pygetwindow path, but awareness does not use it, and pygetwindow is not in requirements.txt.
gaps.evidence: agent/awareness.py:83-99; agent/guardian.py:101-170 (window_title drives MESSAGE/SHOPPING/CALENDAR/COMMIT_TITLE); agent/app_context.py:6; requirements.txt (no pygetwindow)
gaps.fix_hint: Add a Windows branch (ctypes GetForegroundWindow + GetWindowTextW, no extra dependency) to ActiveWindowWatcher, with a fake-based test.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read agent/awareness.py:83-99 (only xdotool, exceptions swallowed). grep -rn 'GetForegroundWindow|win32gui' agent tools app found nothing. No test covers ActiveWindowWatcher.

gaps.issue: Every clipboard copy (first 200 characters, including passwords and API keys) is stored forever in the SQLite perception log and sent to the cloud model in the 60-second proactive review. Guardian even recognises secrets (SENSITIVE_CLIPBOARD), but nothing redacts them before they are stored or sent, and the perception log has no retention limit.
gaps.evidence: agent/awareness.py:116-122 and :50-59 (AwarenessLog.add -> perception.log_event); agent/perception.py:68-78 (plain INSERT, no DELETE/prune anywhere); agent/awareness.py:420-438 (summary sent to model); agent/guardian.py:67-70
gaps.fix_hint: Run SENSITIVE_CLIPBOARD (and a password-manager window check) before log.add, store '[redacted secret]' instead, and add a retention prune (for example 30 days) for perception_log.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the add/log_event code path. grep for 'DELETE|prune|retention' in agent/perception.py found only the FTS trigger and no prune.

gaps.issue: Resident mode (your real launcher) refuses every action that needs a safety confirmation, with no way to say yes. Asking Celine by voice or chat to register a tool, change her prompt or revert self-mod is always blocked. Approving a staged cortex 'sms_send', or a risky bash/write_file, in the Approvals tab still runs through safety.check and is refused again.
gaps.evidence: app/resident.py:138-159 (resident_confirm returns False), :252; agent/safety.py:23-25 (self-mod rules match everything), :84-127; agent/cortex.py:171-174 (approved actions go through core._execute_tool -> safety.check at agent/core.py:2470)
gaps.fix_hint: Treat a dashboard approval as the confirmation (pass an 'already approved' flag through approve_action), and route resident confirmations to a companion or dashboard prompt instead of an automatic NO.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read resident_confirm and safety.check. Confirmed approve_action calls cortex._execute_tool, which calls agent.core._execute_tool, whose inner dispatcher calls safety.check first (agent/core.py:2455-2471). The dashboard Self-mod routes (dashboard/server.py:552-564) bypass this, so that workaround exists.

gaps.issue: Resident mode skips several startup jobs that main.py installs: the weekly self-evaluation (Mon 08:00), the nightly reflection job (03:00), the morning-briefing re-install, the Skill Curator thread, constellation.init(), the orchestrator sub-agent factory, and dash.set_guardian/set_timecapsule. You only run resident mode, so these never start unless main.py was run once on the same database.
gaps.evidence: main.py:285-380 and :414-417 vs app/resident.py:165-320; grep for 'Weekly self|Nightly reflection|install_briefing|curator|set_guardian|set_timecapsule|orchestrator' in app/resident.py found no matches
gaps.fix_hint: Move these into one shared boot helper (like awareness.build_monitor) that both main.py and app/resident.py call, and add a test that both paths install the same scheduled jobs.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran grep -nE on app/resident.py for each of these names: no hits. Read main.py:225-420. Note: reflection consolidation still runs in resident mode via the awareness loop (agent/awareness.py:397-410), so only the scheduled 'Nightly reflection' prompt job is missing.

gaps.issue: The Council and Compare can never run on your setup if DeepSeek is your only key. gaps.issue: Several modules have no tests or no page check: agent/briefing.py (no test imports it), agent/eval.py (no entry point), missions.js (no scripts/check_*.cjs), and ActiveWindowWatcher.
gaps.evidence: grep of tests/ for 'briefing' only hits constellation's convene_briefing; ls scripts/check_*.cjs shows none for missions

needs_from_owner: Re-run Start-Apex-Platform.cmd after the UTF-8 fix and confirm resident.log shows 'Autonomous cortex + awareness monitor started (resident).'
Start Docker Desktop before using Missions with command checks, Skill Forge, or cortex run_python; without Docker these are skipped or refused.
Say which API keys are in .env (ANTHROPIC/OPENAI/GEMINI/DEEPSEEK/OPENROUTER). With DeepSeek only, Council and Compare cannot run.
If you want the morning briefing, enable it in the Briefing tab and set the timezone to Asia/Beirut.
Set at least one goal and watch whether the cortex stages or runs anything in the Approvals tab over an hour.
Run one small real mission on /missions (a file/contains check) to prove the loop on the laptop.
Decide whether you are comfortable with clipboard contents being stored and sent to the model; if not, set AWARENESS_ENABLED=false until redaction is added.

rating.why: There is lots of real, well-tested code, but on your Windows resident setup the window watching is blind, secrets are logged, Council needs keys you may not have, and resident mode silently refuses or skips several autonomy paths.
